cases.design_tool: A tool claims it helps create complete websites. The current marketing opening contains five small isolated widgets; none lets visitors inspect a whole website. A complete authored teaching example is available, but no independent benchmark is available.
cases.service: A local emergency plumbing service. A visitor has an active leak and needs to know service coverage, call availability and how to contact the team. Work photos exist.
cases.store: A returning customer on a furniture shops collection page wants to compare available chairs by size, material and price. Product photos and inventory are available.

state.hypothesis: Scale demonstration evidence to the scope of the specific claim, without imposing showcase-first on every website.

design_tool.instructions: For the visitor task in `cases.design_tool`, which structure should lead? Judge suitability of information order, not unseen visual quality. Do not apply the hypothesis if it adds friction to this task.

criteria.prominent_example: Give a substantial, clearly labeled completed example an early readable position, with access to its full path. Use smaller demonstrations for distinct details.
criteria.action_first: Lead with the immediate action and essential eligibility/availability information; keep examples secondary.
criteria.catalog_first: Lead with a browsable catalog of available items and practical selection controls; show product details on demand.
criteria.none: None of these structures addresses this brief.
